outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Role of Reinforcement Learning in Scaling LLMs
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage for the textbook by discussing the critical role of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in advancing Large Language Models (LLMs). It introduces the context of the research paper, highlighting the shift towards using RL for sophisticated reasoning tasks and the challenges associated with training stability.
subtopics: The paradigm shift: Using RL to enhance reasoning in LLMs
The importance of stability in large-scale RL training
Overview of model collapse and irreversible training failures
Introduction to Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO)

outline.chapter_title: Background: Foundations of PPO and GRPO
outline.description: This chapter provides a necessary review of the precursor algorithms to GSPO. It explains Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), focusing on their mathematical formulations and operational mechanisms, specifically highlighting their use of token-level importance ratios.
subtopics: Autoregressive language models as policies
Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and the clipping mechanism
The reliance on value models in PPO
Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and group-based advantages
Token-level importance ratios in existing methods

outline.chapter_title: Motivation: The Instability of Token-Level Optimization
outline.description: This chapter delves into the theoretical motivation behind GSPO. It critiques the fundamental flaws in GRPO's design, specifically the misapplication of importance sampling weights at the token level. It explains how this leads to high-variance noise and model collapse, establishing the need for a sequence-level approach.
subtopics: The off-policy learning setting in LLM training
The principle of importance sampling
The invalidity of token-level importance weights
Accumulation of variance in long sequences
The core principle: Aligning the unit of optimization with the unit of reward

outline.description: This chapter presents the core contribution of the paper: the Group Sequence Policy Optimization algorithm. It details the mathematical formulation of GSPO, including the definition of sequence-level importance ratios and the modified clipping mechanism.
subtopics: Defining the sequence-level importance ratio
Length normalization of importance ratios
Sequence-level clipping and optimization
Group-based advantage estimation
GSPO-token: A variant for token-level advantage customization

outline.description: This chapter provides a rigorous gradient analysis to justify the superiority of GSPO. It compares the gradient computations of GSPO and GRPO, demonstrating how GSPO's equal weighting of tokens contrasts with GRPO's unstable, unequal weighting.
subtopics: Derivation of the GSPO gradient
Derivation of the GRPO gradient
Comparative analysis: Equal vs. unequal token weighting
Theoretical explanation for reduced variance and stability

outline.description: This chapter covers the experimental validation of GSPO. It details the setup, benchmarks used, and the comparative performance of GSPO against GRPO. It also discusses counter-intuitive findings regarding clipping fractions.
subtopics: Experimental setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base and benchmarks
Training stability and performance curves
Analysis of clipping fractions: Why clipping more tokens leads to better efficiency
Comparison of training efficiency and compute consumption

outline.chapter_title: Advanced Applications: MoE Training and Infrastructure
outline.description: This chapter explores specific practical benefits of GSPO, particularly for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models and RL infrastructure design. It explains how GSPO inherently solves stability issues in MoE training and simplifies system architecture.
subtopics: Stability challenges in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models
Expert-activation volatility and its impact on token-level ratios
Eliminating the need for 'Routing Replay' strategies
Infrastructure simplification: Handling precision discrepancies between training and inference engines
The future of scalable RL with GSPO
